possibleWorlds.name: Admin Role Assigned (Actual)
possibleWorlds.description: Alice currently holds ADMIN_ROLE in the RBAC system. Role policy directly entails obligatory admin access.

possibleWorlds.name: Superadmin Role Assigned
possibleWorlds.description: Alice holds SUPERADMIN_ROLE — a strict superset of ADMIN_ROLE. Policy entails admin access obligatorily.

possibleWorlds.name: Developer + Exceptional Grant
possibleWorlds.description: Alice holds DEVELOPER_ROLE with a time-bounded exceptional admin grant approved by the security team. Grant makes admin access permitted, not obligatory.

possibleWorlds.name: Developer, No Exception
possibleWorlds.description: Alice holds DEVELOPER_ROLE but no exceptional grant has been issued. No entitlement to admin access exists.

possibleWorlds.name: Viewer Role Only
possibleWorlds.description: Alice holds VIEWER_ROLE only — scoped to read-only access. Policy explicitly forbids admin access for this role.

possibleWorlds.name: Account Deactivated
possibleWorlds.description: Alice's account is deactivated (offboarding, suspension, or role revocation). All access permissions are rescinded by policy.

accessibilityRelations.note: S5 frame: reflexivity + euclidean property → equivalence class. All six worlds are mutually accessible.

propositions.content: □(alice_has_admin_access) — Alice MUST have admin access unconditionally
propositions.justification: Falsified by countermodels w4, w5, and w6. In all three accessible worlds, alice_has_admin_access is false (developer without grant, viewer role, deactivated account). Unconditional deontic necessity fails: O(admin_access) does not hold across the full Kripke frame.

Witnessed in w1, w2, and w3. alice_has_admin_access is true in at least one accessible world (three, in fact). Deontic permission holds: P(admin_access) is satisfied. Alice's admin access is permitted but not universally obligated.

propositions.content: □(alice_has_admin_access | alice_has_admin_role ∨ alice_has_superadmin_role) — Alice MUST have admin access given a role-level entitlement
propositions.justification: In every world within the sub-frame {w1, w2} — the role-entitlement worlds — alice_has_admin_access holds. Role policy acts as a deontic axiom: ADMIN_ROLE → O(admin_access). Conditional necessity is satisfied; the obligation is role-triggered, not universal. This is the 'MUST' answer: Alice's obligation is role-relative.

propositions.content: ◇(alice_has_admin_access | alice_has_developer_role) — Alice COULD have admin access while a developer
propositions.justification: Witnessed by w3 (developer + exceptional grant). However, w4 (developer, no grant) falsifies necessity. Therefore: developer role alone permits admin access only when an exceptional grant is active. P(admin_access | developer ∧ exceptional_grant) holds; O(admin_access | developer) does not.

propositions.content: □¬(alice_has_admin_access | alice_account_deactivated) — Alice MUST NOT have admin access when deactivated
propositions.justification: In all worlds accessible from w6 (and w6 itself in S5), alice_lacks_admin_access holds. Deontic prohibition is a necessity over negation: F(admin_access) = O(¬admin_access) = □¬admin_access in the deactivated sub-frame. Granting admin access to a deactivated account would be a deontic violation.

propositions.content: □¬(alice_has_admin_access | alice_has_viewer_role) — Alice MUST NOT have admin access as a viewer
propositions.justification: In w5, VIEWER_ROLE → F(admin_access) is a hard policy constraint. No accessible world from w5 permits admin access for the viewer role. This is a role-ceiling prohibition: the role cap forecloses even exceptional grants.

propositions.content: ◇¬(alice_has_admin_access) — It is possible (permitted by the frame) that Alice lacks admin access
propositions.justification: Witnessed by w4, w5, and w6. This is the dual confirmation of p1's failure: since □(admin_access) is false, ◇¬(admin_access) must be true (S5 duality). The RBAC system permits states where Alice has no admin access.

premises: O(P) → P is true in all deontically accessible worlds [Necessitation in deontic D/S5]
inferences.conclusion: In worlds w1 and w2, Alice MUST (is obligated to) have admin access. This is conditional necessity: □(admin_access) restricted to the sub-frame {w1, w2}.
inferences.justification: Necessitation rule: if P follows from the normative axioms of the frame (here, the RBAC role policy), then O(P) holds. The role policy is a deontic axiom, so it necessitates the permission in all role-bearing worlds.

premises: w4 is accessible from w1 [S5 mutual accessibility]
inferences.conclusion: Unconditional □(alice_has_admin_access) is FALSE. Three independent countermodels exist. The access obligation is not a universal truth of the RBAC frame — it is role-gated.
inferences.justification: Countermodel argument: □P is false iff there exists at least one accessible world where P is false. Here three such worlds exist, decisively ruling out unconditional necessity.

premises: alice_has_admin_access is false in w4 (developer, no grant)
inferences.conclusion: P(admin_access | developer_role) is true (w3 witnesses it), but O(admin_access | developer_role) is false (w4 is a countermodel). Developer admin access is permissible under exceptional grant, not obligatory.
inferences.justification: S5 T-axiom applied to sub-frame: ◇P is true if P holds in one accessible world (w3). Necessity fails because the full developer sub-frame {w3, w4} contains a falsifying world (w4). This grounds the distinction between permission and obligation.

premises: Deontic axiom D: O(P) → P(P) [obligation entails permission]
In w1 and w2: O(admin_access) holds
inferences.conclusion: In worlds w1 and w2, Alice's admin access is both obligatory AND permitted. The system must grant it and Alice is entitled to it. Refusing to grant admin in these worlds is a deontic violation of the RBAC policy.
inferences.justification: Axiom D (the defining axiom of deontic logic): □P → ◇P. Obligation implies permission. This rules out deontic inconsistency — we cannot simultaneously obligate P and forbid P.

premises: O(P) and F(P) are jointly inconsistent in deontic logic [¬(O(P) ∧ O(¬P))]
inferences.conclusion: If Alice's account is deactivated, granting admin access is a deontic contradiction. No role assignment in a deactivated state can create an obligation to grant admin. Deactivation is a deontic ceiling that overrides all role-based obligations.
inferences.justification: Deontic consistency: O(P) ∧ O(¬P) is inconsistent in any standard deontic system (D, S5). Since deactivation imposes O(¬admin), no simultaneous O(admin) can hold. The prohibition takes precedence by policy supremacy.
